description: Three-panel composite figure (all panels are data plots) used to select features for machine-learning prediction of microhardness in Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel. (a) is a rank heatmap: rows are the three selection methods XGBoost, RF and LightGBM (labelled "Selection methods"); the 38 columns are candidate features (VEC, Tm, e/a, G, E, Ec, ω, r, χ, B, EI-1st, EI-2nd, ΔSmix, ΔHmix, Δχ, δ, ηB, δG, δB, δv, δr, ΔTm, δEc, δE/a, δEI-1st, δEI-2nd, ΔG, DB, Dv, Dr, DTm, DVEC, De/a, DEc, DEI-1st, DEI-2nd, γ, BX), x-axis "Candidate features"; each cell prints the RFE rank (small integers, up to 22), dark blue cells = rank 1 (significant), and red stars sit above roughly six columns. (b) is a 9×9 Pearson-correlation matrix over e/a, G, ω, EI-2nd, ηB, δEc, δEI-2nd, DEc, γ, drawn as circles sized and coloured by PCC with a colour bar from blue (+1) through white (0) to red (-1); printed numbers fill the lower triangle. (c) is a bar chart of "Importance score" (y-axis, 0–0.5, tick every 0.1) versus "Features", legend "Ranking by importance". Together they argue that redundant descriptors are removed and a compact key-feature set drives hardness.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a heatmap in which the three rows are the selection methods XGBoost, RF and LightGBM and the columns are 38 candidate features, from VEC to BX, each cell carrying an integer RFE rank.
Dark-blue cells (printed value 1) in panel (a) mark the significant features per algorithm, and red stars are placed above approximately six of the columns.
Panel (b) is a 9x9 PCC matrix over the labels e/a, G, ω, EI-2nd, ηB, δEc, δEI-2nd, DEc and γ, with a colour bar from +1 (blue) through 0 (white) to -1 (red).
Printed PCC values in panel (b) reach -1.00 and 1.00: ηB vs EI-2nd is -1.00, δEI-2nd vs ηB is 1.00, δEI-2nd vs EI-2nd is -1.00, and DEc vs δEc is 1.00.
Other large printed PCC magnitudes in panel (b) include ω vs ηB 0.98, ω vs δEc 0.92, ω vs δEI-2nd 0.97, ω vs DEc 0.94, δEI-2nd vs δEc 0.83, δEI-2nd vs DEc 0.86 and G vs e/a -0.89.
The γ row of panel (b) shows strong negative correlations, printed as -0.96 with δEc, -0.95 with DEc, -0.78 with ηB, -0.85 with ω and -0.75 with δEI-2nd.

Panel (c) ranks nine feature importance scores: EI-2nd is the tallest bar (between the 0.4 and 0.5 gridlines), ηB is the second tallest (just below 0.15), and the bars for DEc, δEc, γ, G and e/a are all at or below the 0.05 gridline.
The caption states that (a) is feature selection by RFE voting, (b) is a heatmap showing the PCC between the 9 features, and (c) is the importance ranking of the 9 features.

The citing text reports that RFE wrapped RF, LightGBM and XGBoost to rank the original features, and that dark-blue cells (value 1) mark significant features, with E_I-2nd, η, w, δE, D, δ, r, G and e/a obtaining the highest importance ranking in all three algorithms.

The citing text states that six feature pairs have |PCC| >= 0.95 (E and w, ηB and w, E_I-2nd and ηB, r and D_EC, E_I-2nd and δE_I-2nd, δE_I-2nd and ηB), and that one member of each pair with the lower importance score (ηB, w, δE_I-2nd and r) was removed, leaving e/a, G, E, δ and D_EC as key features.

The citing text asserts that e/a < 1.65 favours the FCC phase while e/a > 2.05 favours the BCC phase, and that G raises the resistance to plastic deformation via solute atom-dislocation interaction energy.

The axes of panel (b) list ω and G, not 'w' and 'E', although the citing text refers to correlated pairs 'E and w'; the label correspondence between the text and the plotted heatmap is therefore not fully consistent, and the image alone does not confirm the text's symbol naming.

subfigures.description: RFE voting rank heatmap. Three rows (XGBoost, RF, LightGBM) against 38 candidate-feature columns (VEC ... BX). Each cell contains an integer rank; dark-blue cells (rank 1) are the significant features. Red stars mark about six columns favoured by the voting scheme. Individual cell digits are only partially legible at the supplied resolution.

9x9 Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) matrix over e/a, G, ω, EI-2nd, ηB, δEc, δEI-2nd, DEc, γ. Upper triangle = filled circles whose size and colour encode PCC; lower triangle prints the numeric PCC values (e.g. G-e/a -0.89, EI-2nd-ω -0.98, ηB-EI-2nd -1.00, δEI-2nd-ηB 1.00, DEc-δEc 1.00, γ-δEc -0.96). Colour bar runs blue (+1) through white (0) to red (-1).

Bar chart of feature importance score (y-axis 0-0.5) for nine features ordered EI-2nd, ηB, ω, δEI-2nd, DEc, δEc, γ, G, e/a; legend 'Ranking by importance'. The EI-2nd bar exceeds the 0.4 gridline but not 0.5, ηB is just below 0.15, ω and δEI-2nd near 0.13 and 0.10, and the remaining five bars (DEc, δEc, γ, G, e/a) all fall at or below the 0.05 gridline.
